notes: Adds a `StandardDiffPrefixes` builder that pins noprefix, mnemonicPrefix and src/dst prefixes on every diff lazygit parses or applies, including the previously unpinned worktree file diff and stash show commands; it also strips any single-component header prefix, prefers `rename to`/`copy to` over `--- `, and passes the hidden tests. The truncated `diff --git` splitting and any new parser tests could not be checked, and the visible test changes only update expected command lines mechanically.

C1 fixes the bug from both sides and passes the hidden tests. A `StandardDiffPrefixes()` builder forces a/ and b/ prefixes (noprefix, mnemonicPrefix, srcPrefix, dstPrefix) on every diff lazygit reads back, including worktree and stash diffs, and the header parser now strips any single-component prefix and prefers `rename to`/`copy to` paths. Two things could not be checked: the `diff --git` split logic is in the truncated part of the diff, and the shown test changes only update expected command args with no new parser tests visible. Forcing a/ and b/ on rendered diffs also overrides the user's mnemonic display preference, though this is defensible.

Fixes both root causes: a reusable caller with unfinished children now stays Cancelling so the runner's acknowledgement can cascade up to the run, and a cancel that updates no jobs now re-checks the run's concurrency groups so blocked runs start. The caller fix checks only direct children at cancel time, so it relies on processing order or an existing upward cascade, and its 'one level is enough' comment states this assumption without proving it. The tests are good: a nested caller test exercises the full runner-acknowledgement handshake, and a service test covers force-cancel waking the waiter, though it builds the child with ParentJobID=0 because caller.ID is read before the caller is inserted.

Fixes both root causes: a reusable caller now stays Cancelling while any direct child is unfinished, so the runner's acknowledgement cascades up, and force-cancelling an already-settled run now triggers a concurrency re-check; the tests cover the nested-caller handshake end to end and the waiter wake-up, though the one-level child check silently depends on CancelJobs cancelling children before their callers.

Correctly fixes the root cause: placeholder names are collected from the checked CEL AST, so escaped text, the `{}` shorthand, direct `ph()` calls and dynamic names are all handled as the maintainers specified, and only real response placeholders (status, headers, latency) trigger response-based retries; it adds a small exported `Placeholders()` API on `MatchExpression` and strong unit and end-to-end tests covering every listed case.

Fixes the root cause robustly: it collects `ph()` placeholder names from the type-checked CEL AST, so both the shorthand and direct `ph()` calls are covered, escaped or string-literal look-alikes are ignored, and dynamic names are conservatively treated as response conditions. It then matches only exact status/text/latency names or the `header.` prefix. Tests cover the AST extraction, the classification table and end-to-end retry behaviour; the only cost is a small new exported API (`Placeholders()`) on `MatchExpression`.

The patch tracks the latest exemplar timestamp on memSeries, using a hasExemplar flag so zero and negative timestamps count. Ordinary GC retains the series without holding back actualMint, and selected/stale GC frees chunks, clears the appender and keeps mmapReady and the chunk metrics consistent; replay/snapshot restoration falls in the truncated part of the diff and could not be inspected, though the extensive restart tests and hidden tests pass. Drawbacks are a side-effecting shouldEvict wrapper and an unrelated rewrite of the colliding-series test helper.

Tracks per-series exemplar timestamps (with a hasExemplar flag, so zero and negative timestamps count) and retains the series identity in both ordinary gc and selected/stale gcSeries until the replay cutoff passes, releasing chunks and the appender and keeping chunk metrics and mmap-ready accounting consistent. The tests cover all three compaction modes, both appenders, snapshot, double restart and concurrent appends; minor reservations are the conservative protection from rolled-back exemplars, an unrelated refactor of the stripeSeriesWithCollidingSeries test helper, and replay/snapshot restoration that falls in the truncated part of the diff and could not be checked.

Fixes the root cause: it no longer leaks a dup'd fd via File() in Close, and it closes socketFile in the reuse path. It unlinks the real Addr() path only when the last reference closes, and it serializes close and relisten under unixSocketsMu so racing reloads stay safe. It returns net.ErrClosed on a double close and skips unlinking on both listen and close for Linux abstract sockets. Tests cover all of this thoroughly, with minor nits: the abstract-socket test creates a sentinel file in the package directory, and one test calls reuseUnixSocket without holding the mutex.

The patch fixes the real cause: `Close` no longer calls `File()`, whose duplicated fd kept the socket listening until GC and whose 'unix:/path->' name made unlink fail. It now closes the duplicated `socketFile` in the reuse path and unlinks via `Addr().String()`. It also covers every review requirement (double close returns `net.ErrClosed`, unlink only at refcount zero, close and relisten serialized under `unixSocketsMu`, no unlink for abstract `@` sockets) and adds thorough tests for both stream and datagram sockets.

The zip and squashfs symlink handling is clean: symlinks are skipped with a notice naming `-l/--links`, exposed with the `.rclonelink` suffix and read back as their target, and squashfs `NewObject` names entries the same way `List` does. However, nothing stops a hostile archive from escaping the destination; the patch relies on the local backend failing. That failure only happens when the symlink target does not exist, which is the only case the new test covers. If the target directory exists and the root-level symlink is transferred first (the likely order), `a/pwned.txt` is written outside the destination. Smaller gaps: no handling of name collisions between a symlink and a regular `X.rclonelink`, no squashfs single-file root at a `.rclonelink` path, and no range/seek tests.

Zip and squashfs both follow the spec cleanly. Symlinks are skipped with a notice naming -l/--links, exposed as name+.rclonelink with target-length size and range-aware reads, NewObject agrees with List, and regular .rclonelink members stay regular files. However, the zip side still exposes members beneath a symlink entry (e.g. `a.rclonelink` plus `a/pwned.txt`) and leaves escape protection to the local destination; the escape test only passes because its `../outside` target is dangling, so a link to an existing directory like `..` may still escape.

The core fix looks right: `Close` is on the interface, the plugin closes the agent's connection after a field or table failure, `Get`/`Walk` reconnect a closed connection, and reconnecting clears the engine ID, boots, time and `ContextEngineID` so discovery runs again. However, it restores user-configured engine values instead of always forcing fresh discovery, may close several times in one gather, adds unkeyed-literal-breaking struct fields, and makes an unrelated environment workaround to `TestSnmpInitGosmi`, which together plausibly explain one failing hidden test and the failed package suite.

The fix covers the spec: `Close` is added to the interface, the plugin closes the agent's connection after any field or table failure, and a closed-connection `Reconnect` resets the USM engine ID, boots, time and `ContextEngineID` before reconnecting, with `Get`/`Walk` reconnecting first. However, it restores user-configured engine values instead of always forcing fresh discovery, likely behind 1 of 2 hidden PR tests and the package suite failing. It also rewrites the unrelated `TestSnmpInitGosmi` (path handling and Logger), which is scope creep.
